purpose: Independent verification requested by root of existing R4R source originals. Root owns A8 source catalogue and integration; this file does not allocate duplicate R4H claims.
method: Read original PDFs and text. Visually checked all 23 original Letters Patent witness clauses, plus Fort Nelson 1958 and 1959; visually checked material name/governance ambiguities and the 1969 transfer schedule. The PDF boundaries were read as legal descriptions but not mapped.

conditions: Eligible to register as a voter under the Provincial Elections Act
Owner of land within the relevant district or electoral zone, or authorized agent of a board/corporation that owns such land, or a specified legal representative of a landowner
common_elector_profile.legal_representatives_as_described: Representatives of an owner who has died, become insolvent, or been adjudged within the historical mental-incapacity wording of the instrument.
common_elector_profile.candidate_rule_default: Qualified voters are also eligible trustee candidates, subject to instrument-specific exceptions below.
common_elector_profile.limits: This is the rule in each original Letters Patent at its date. Later amendments were not exhaustively reviewed. It is not a universal provincial-population electorate. Provincial-voter eligibility is a cross-reference, not an independent reconstruction of all residence or franchise exclusions.

statutory_authority.amendment_as_recited: Section 5 of the Water Act Amendment Act, 1953 (Second Session). Most orders also give SBC 1953 (Second Session), c.38.

governance.seat_allocation: Two trustees for zone 3; one for each other zone.
governance.initial_selection: Five first trustees named in the Letters Patent, clause 6; initial board was appointed, not elected.
governance.subsequent_selection: Elections at annual zone meetings; clause 8.
governance.candidate_exception: Hospital employees and physicians actively practising medicine were disqualified as trustee candidates; this clause does not by itself remove a qualified person’s vote.
governance.hospital_board: Trustees plus the Hospital Act s.5 appointee constitute the hospital board of management.

original_incorporation.objects: Hospital services, acquisition, ownership, maintenance and operation of a hospital and related land; clause 3, PDF p.3.

replacement_letters_patent.date_basis: Witness clause at PDF p.6, visually checked; cover approved 7 July 1959.
replacement_letters_patent.continuation_pinpoint: PDF p.2, clause 1 expressly continues incorporation.
replacement_letters_patent.change: Five trustees elected from the district as a whole; zonal allocation removed. Ambulance services added to objects.

governance.candidate_rule: All qualified voters eligible; the prior instrument’s employee/physician candidate exception is absent from this replacement clause.
governance.hospital_board: Trustees plus Hospital Act s.5 appointee constitute hospital board of management (PDF p.3, clause 6).

replacement_letters_patent.limitation: This verifies the replacement clause, not the effect of any separately applicable disqualification in another statute.

dissolution_and_transfer.date_basis: Operative clause expressly makes dissolution effective on the date of the order.

onward_transfer.effective_trigger: As and from the date of dissolution of the improvement district.
onward_transfer.exception: Fundraising, disbursement and long-term debt obligations previously assumed by the regional hospital district remain with it.
onward_transfer.caution: Attached resolution authorizes appropriate conveyances. The actual signed deeds are not attached.

dissolution_and_transfer.society_registration_basis: Order recital, PDF p.1; not an independently retrieved registry certificate.

ambulance_resolution.pinpoint: PDF p.3, hospital society board resolution
ambulance_resolution.effect: Accepts ambulance-service responsibility as ancillary hospital operation; includes insurance commitments and incorporates 26 May 1970 agreement; resolution expires 31 March 1973.

conflicts_and_cautions.finding: Seven original names differ from the 1969 schedule. Six original letters omit the later district number. Windermere also uses Windermere District Hospital; Prince George uses and District. Fraser Canyon later appears hyphenated and numbered.
conflicts_and_cautions.action: Store dated source labels and leave any intervening renaming/numbering date unproved. These differences are not evidence of a separate incorporation.

conflicts_and_cautions.finding: The 1969 North Peace transfer row prints Peace River Regional Hospital District; the 1972 Fort Nelson transfer names Peace River-Liard Regional Hospital District.
conflicts_and_cautions.action: Preserve source wording; do not infer a formal rename from these labels alone.

conflicts_and_cautions.finding: Handwritten witness dates read 14 May 1955, 4 October 1955 and 9 December 1955 respectively. Text extraction is unreliable for these entries.
Fort Nelson began 7 June 1958. Its 7 July 1959 letters expressly continued the incorporation; they did not start a new entity.
conflicts_and_cautions.action: Represent a continuation/governance change, then the 13 June 1972 dissolution and transfer.

conflicts_and_cautions.finding: Landowner and representative voting qualifications, spouse candidate provisions and occupation-based candidate exceptions differ across instruments.
conflicts_and_cautions.action: Do not collapse these into a modern universal electorate or treat candidate exclusions as voter exclusions.
